texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 22.05.2023. 2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that on 22.05.2023 at about 10.30 p.m., petitioner was proceeding as rider in his motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-KK-5434 on BEL Underpass, Mes Ring Road, Jalahalli, Bangalore i.e., from Gorguntepalya and proceeding towards Hebbal. He was riding his motorcycle slowly and cautiously and observing all the traffic rules and riding on the extreme left side of the road, when he reached near BEL Circle underpass, at that time a Car bearing Reg.No. KA-04-MR-8783 being driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner without giving any hand signal or indicator and suddenly stopped his Car on the middle of the underpass, endangering to human life, where there is no place for parking the vehicle, caused interrupting other traffic vehicles with negligent manner. Due to the sudden negligent act of the car driver the petitioner fell down from his Scooter and sustained grievous injuries to his face and head. Immediately, he was shifted to M. S. Ramaiah Memorial Hospital for first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to M. S. Ramaiah Medical College and Hospital, Bangalore wherein he was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment expenses. The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 25 years, the petitioner was working as Assistant Manager at Teamlease Pvt. Ltd., (Swiggy Insta Mart), Hebbal, Bangalore and earning salary of Rs.30,000/- per month with overtime salary. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled. Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest. Sandesha.R vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 25 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13196527/ 2 3. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared through his counsel and filed the written statement. Respondent No.2 has not appeared before the Court and he remained placed exparte. The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle. He also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. The respondent No.1 further submitted that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident. The petitioner colluding with a owner and police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.24 and examined MRD Technician at Ramaiah Memorial Hospital as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.25 to Ex.P.27 and examined Senior Executive at Scootsy Logistics Pvt. Ltd., as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.28 to Ex.P.32 and examined Dr. Shailesh A. V. Rao as PW.4 and got marked documents at Ex.P.33 to Ex.P.35 and also examined MRD at M. S. Ramaiah Medical College Hospital, Bangalore as PW.5 and got marked documents at Ex.P.36 to Ex.P38 and closed their side. On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of the respondents.
texts.arguments: 14. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. The learned counsel for petitioner quoted decision of Hon'ble High court of Karnataka, Bangalore in MFA NO.1419/2023 between H. P. Nagegowda and Subramanya Kalluraya, wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that, 'tribunal has to accept the evidence of neuro-surgoen when the mental faculties of a person is involved'. The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses. In support of his plea, he has produced 41 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.23 to the tune of Rs.1,71,021/-. The petitioner is entitled for the amount spent for purchasing the medicine. During the course of argument, learned counsel for petitioner argued that due to injury marriage prospectus of petitioner have been diminished. Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.50,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness as well as marriage prospectus. Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads: 1 Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/- 2 As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%. By relying on the aforesaid decision, Sandesha.R vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 25 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13196527/ 8 6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand.
